explanation:
[EFFECT] Hour of the day has a non-monotonic effect: very early morning hours (midnight to roughly 4 a.m.) deliver the largest negative contributions, dramatically pulling predicted demand down, while mid-to-late daytime and evening hours push demand up. The relationship is not a simple climb — contributions vary across the full 24-hour cycle — but the clearest signal is that night hours strongly suppress and peak-use hours strongly boost rentals.
[IMPORTANCE] This is by far the most important feature in the model, with a horizontal spread roughly four times wider than any other feature; no other variable comes close.

---
[RECOMMENDATION] Staffing and bike-redistribution plans should be driven primarily by the **hour of the day** — which overwhelmingly determines whether a given hour will be busy or quiet — and secondarily by **temperature**, since warm spells can substantially lift demand even in off-peak hours. Scheduling more bikes and staff during warm, mid-to-late day hours will capture the greatest share of predicted demand variation.
